name: Pendulum Squat
grip: Hands gripping support handles on machine shoulder harness.
description: Perform a guided squat on a counterweighted pendulum machine along a curved arc that maximizes knee flexion and quad loading while minimizing lumbar stress.
setup: Load weight plates onto the machine's counterbalanced pendulum horn.
Step onto the angled footplate with feet shoulder-width apart.
Position shoulders snugly under the padded harness and back resting flat against the pivoting back support.
Release the safety latch and stand tall with knees softly unlocked.
instructions: Descend smoothly by flexing knees and hips, allowing the pendulum arm to swing backward along its curved arc.
Lower until thighs reach parallel to the footplate or full knee flexion is achieved, keeping back flat against the pad.
Pause briefly at the bottom under complete muscular control.
Drive through the mid-foot to push back up along the pendulum arc to the starting position without forcefully locking knees.
cues: Keep back flat against the pad.
Track knees over toes along the arc.
commonMistakes: Letting lower back or pelvis lift off the back support at depth.
Locking knees aggressively at the top.
Bouncing out of the bottom position.

logging.example: Two 20 kg plates on weight horn: record 40 kg total plate load.
logging.note: Pendulum squat machines feature counterweights and curved mechanical leverage arcs; record total loaded plate mass rather than attempting free barbell equivalency.

variantNote: Guided squat on a counterweighted pendulum machine with angled footplate and pivoting back support.
